description: We are university students with enthusiasm in astronomy and programming.
summary: An interactive web tool was developed to query infrared image data from NASA's SPHEREx mission and to display data as a single image or as a series of images of the same sky region but taken at different time. A number of interactive tools were made for adjustments of image visualisation. In Multi-epoch mode (time sequence images), user can also select images to be viewed individually or as an animation. This tool can be used to search for objects moving relative to distant celestial objects by comparing images at different epochs. With the infrared images, it is of particular advantage for the search of faint objects including brown dwarfs, comets and potentially a planet.
details:
The frontend uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, served through GitHub Pages. It provides the dashboard, image controls, observation selection, and timeline player. Brightness adjustments and playback run in the browser after data is loaded. User can zoom/pan images and change the brightness stretch and range of sky coordinates to be displayed.

The backend uses Python and FastAPI, hosted on Render. It validates requests, queries SIA, processes FITS images, applies quality masks, reprojects multi-epoch frames, and caches rendered results. The Astropy package was used for image processing, and the python imaging library Pillow was used for PNG rendering.

The aim of this project is to develop an image viewing web tool which is easy to use and accessible to the public. The search for faint celestial bodies requires people to examine the tremendous amount of data obtained by modern observatories. The time it takes for researchers to look through all the data is usually impractical. Therefore, by inviting people, either scientists or non-scientists, to help searching moving objects in the sky using the web tool, the collective efforts of crowds can make a huge impact like many existing astronomical citizen projects.
